author: Navjot Tomer (Mindstellar)
description_html:
Digital Goods

Lets a seller attach downloadable files to a listing (a manual, an ebook, a sample pack). Buyers get them through a download link that checks who may have them.

Requirements

  • Shopclass 7.0.0 or later, tested up to 7.1
  • PHP 8.0 or later, with the fileinfo extension (on by default)
  • Optional: S3 storage, set up in core under Settings → Storage

Install

  1. Open Plugins → Browse (or upload the zip from the GitHub release).
  2. Install.
  3. Activate.

Or run php oc-cli.php market:install digital-goods.

Set up

  1. Open Billing → Digital Goods (Plugins → Digital Goods on cores before 7.1).
  2. Under Categories, pick the categories that take files.
  3. Under Files, set Who can download, Files per listing (1 to 20), Largest file (MB) and File types.
  4. Optional, under Charging: tick Charge sellers to attach files and set Credits per listing. It is off by default.
  5. Save. Files now appear on the post and edit forms and on the listing page.

Billing → Downloads lists every attached file, its listing and its download count.

How it works

  • Uploads are stored under a random key. Nothing about where a file is kept comes from the uploader. The download address is a separate random token.
  • Every download goes through the download link, which applies the access rule and counts the fetch.
  • Who can download has four choices:
    • Signed-in visitors (default)
    • Anyone
    • Anyone who bought it, and the seller: needs a paid order for the listing (Shopclass 7.0 shop mode). Pending, cancelled and refunded orders do not count.
    • The seller only
  • The seller can always download their own files.
  • Charging: sellers spend credits per listing, like a bump or highlight. Listings that already have files keep them. Only the seller pays. Buyers pay for the listing through the shop.

Storage

StorageWhere files goDelivery
Local (default)oc-content/downloads/digital-goods/, closed to the webthe link streams the file
S3 with signed URLsthe bucketthe link redirects to a signed URL that lasts 5 minutes
S3, public bucketthe bucketthe link streams the file

A public bucket serves a file to anyone who has its address. The link never shows that address, but use signed URLs for private files. The settings screen warns when a public bucket is in use.

Allowed file types

An upload must match its claimed extension when the file is examined. Only these can be offered: zip, 7z, gz, tgz, rar, pdf, epub, mp3, wav, mp4, png, jpg, svg, txt, csv. The default is zip,7z,gz,pdf,epub. Anything else typed into File types is dropped on save.

The size limit is also capped by what PHP accepts (upload_max_filesize).

Notes / limits

  • nginx: Apache gets an .htaccess that denies the folder. nginx ignores it, so add this to your server block (Shopclass's Docker images already have it):
    location ^~ /oc-content/downloads/ {
    deny all;
}
  • Private folder: to keep files out of the web root, set this in config.php before files are uploaded, or move the digital-goods folder there:
    define('DG_PRIVATE_PATH', '/var/lib/shopclass-files');
  • Faster downloads (optional): PHP streams files in chunks and answers byte ranges. To let the web server send the file instead, use one of these in config.php.

    nginx:

    location ^~ /dg-private/ {
    internal;
    alias /path/to/site/oc-content/downloads/digital-goods/;
}
    define('DG_ACCEL_REDIRECT', '/dg-private/');

    Apache with mod_xsendfile (XSendFilePath set to the folder):

    define('DG_XSENDFILE', true);
  • Upgrading from 2.0.x: local files lived in oc-content/uploads/digital-goods/, which the web server serves. On the first request after the upgrade the plugin moves them to the new folder and closes the old one with an .htaccess. Download links do not change. A file that cannot be moved is still served, and the move is retried. On nginx you can also deny the old folder:
    location ^~ /oc-content/uploads/digital-goods/ {
    deny all;
}
  • Stored data: one table, t_item_dg_file (listing, random key, download token, name, size, type, download count). Settings are preferences in the digital_goods section.
  • Uninstall deletes the files, the table and the settings.

For developers

  • Actions: init, item_form, item_edit, item_detail, posted_item, edited_item, delete_item, admin_menu_init, api_listings_prefetch.
  • Filters: api_listing, cart_needs_shipping (a cart of downloads asks for no address), billing_receipt_details (adds download links to the paid receipt), user_menu_filter.
  • On Shopclass 7.0, API listings carry ext.digital-goods.downloads: [{name, url}] for callers the rule lets in, an empty list for everyone else.

Support

https://github.com/mindstellar/shopclass-plugin-digital-goods/issues

License

GPL-3.0-or-later. Derived from the Osclass "Digital Goods" plugin (1.1.0, 2013), originally Apache-2.0. Both notices are kept in the source headers. See CHANGELOG.md for what changed.

versions.changelog_html:
New

  • A Downloads page in the buyer's account lists the files from paid orders, newest first, with a Downloads entry in the account menu once the buyer has one.

Changed

  • The settings page uses core's settings form, with the standard Save bar.
  • The Downloads page uses core's table, page title and empty state.
  • Menu entries read Settings and Downloads under the Digital Goods heading.
  • Shorter help text on every setting.
  • Needs Shopclass 6.4.0 or newer.

Fixed

  • Categories are chosen on the plugin's settings page, so a saved choice shows where it was made.
  • The Configure link in the plugin list opens the settings page.
  • A moderator can no longer save the plugin's settings.

Security

  • Local files are stored in oc-content/downloads/digital-goods/, closed to the web, instead of the uploads folder, so a direct URL no longer skips the access rule.
  • Existing files are moved there on upgrade, and the old folder is closed with an .htaccess.

Changed

  • Downloads stream in chunks instead of loading the whole file into memory, and support byte ranges.
  • A private bucket's signed link sets the file name and lasts 5 minutes.
  • Optional DG_PRIVATE_PATH, DG_ACCEL_REDIRECT and DG_XSENDFILE settings in config.php.

First Shopclass release, rewritten from the Osclass plugin (1.1.0, 2013).

Security

  • An upload could run as code on the server. What was accepted was decided from $_FILES[…]['type'] — a header the uploading client writes — and the file was then written under its own submitted name into oc-content/uploads/digitalgoods/, a directory the web server executes. A PHP script announced as application/zip was therefore uploaded, stored and executable. Uploads are now identified by reading the file with fileinfo, the extension has to be one the admin listed and has to agree with what the bytes say, and the stored name is random.
  • The download script served whatever path the caller named. It built a filesystem path by joining the upload directory to the file query parameter and read that, using the database only to decide whether to bother. The parameter is now an opaque token used solely to find a row; the row decides the storage key, the name and the type.
  • There was no access control. Anyone who knew a filename could download the file, and the file was reachable directly by URL in any case, which made the download script, its counter and any notion of who paid entirely optional. Who may download is now a setting, enforced in the one place a file can be obtained.

Changed

  • Files are stored through the storage layer, so a site with remote storage keeps them out of the web root and hands them over with a short-lived signed URL.
  • The download address is a random token separate from the storage key, so the layout of the bucket can change without breaking a published link.
  • Downloads are counted with an UPDATE … i_downloads + 1 rather than read-modify-write, which lost a count whenever two downloads overlapped.
  • Queries go through the query builder with bound values, replacing a model on the legacy DAO that assembled SQL by concatenation.
  • Rows are removed by the listing's foreign key rather than by a cleanup pass, and the stored objects are deleted with the listing.
  • The download endpoint is a registered route, so it runs inside the application instead of reaching for oc-load.php through a fixed number of parent directories.

New

  • Settings for who may download, how many files a listing may carry, the largest file, and the accepted types.
  • An admin screen listing what has been attached and how often each file has been fetched.
  • Attaching files can be sold. Where the billing subsystem is present (Shopclass 6.2.0 and later), it registers as a per-listing upgrade a seller buys with credits, alongside bump and highlight. Off by default, and every entry point is guarded on the subsystem being there, so the plugin still runs — free — on 6.1.0.
  • A warning on the settings screen when files are being stored somewhere the web server hands out directly.

Fixed

  • Uninstall removes the stored files as well as the table and the settings. It previously dropped the table, which was the only record of where the files were, stranding them.
